record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Two-photon exchange as an explanation of Rosenbluth-polarization discrepancy
record.original_question: Is two-photon exchange in elastic electron-proton scattering responsible for the discrepancy between proton electromagnetic form factors extracted by Rosenbluth separation of unpolarized cross-section data and those extracted by the polarization method from the ratio of longitudinal to transverse recoil-proton polarizations?

evidence.quote: For the electric proton FF, the discrepancy among the data measured with the Rosenbluth methods (stars) and the polarization method (solid squares) appears clearly in Fig. 1a.
• is the 2γ exchange the reason of the discrepancy between the FFs measured with the two different methods?
All the considerations and results presented above are based on the assumption that the main reaction mechanism is one-photon exchange, the two-photon contribution being suppressed by the order of α.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In elastic electron–proton scattering $e^- p \to e^- p$, the proton's electromagnetic structure is characterized by the Sachs electric and magnetic form factors $G_E^p(Q^2)$ and $G_M^p(Q^2)$, where $Q^2$ is the squared four-momentum transfer. Under the standard assumption that the reaction proceeds dominantly by one-photon exchange, two experimental methods to extract these form factors are:

(i) the Rosenbluth (longitudinal–transverse) separation, in which the reduced unpolarized differential cross section is written as
$$\sigma_R(Q^2,\varepsilon) \;=\; \tau\, G_M^p(Q^2)^2 \;+\; \varepsilon\, G_E^p(Q^2)^2,$$
with $\tau = Q^2/(4 M_p^2)$ and $\varepsilon$ the virtual-photon longitudinal polarization parameter, and the two form factors are extracted from the linear dependence on $\varepsilon$ at fixed $Q^2$;

(ii) the polarization-transfer method, in which a longitudinally polarized electron beam scatters from an unpolarized proton target and the ratio of the transferred recoil-proton transverse and longitudinal polarization components determines the ratio
$$\frac{G_E^p(Q^2)}{G_M^p(Q^2)} \;\propto\; -\frac{P_t}{P_l}\,\sqrt{\frac{\tau(1+\varepsilon)}{2\varepsilon}}.$$

At momentum transfers $Q^2$ of a few GeV$^2$ and above, these two methods yield significantly different results for $G_E^p/G_M^p$.

Beyond one-photon exchange, the next correction is the two-photon exchange (TPE) amplitude, suppressed nominally by one power of the fine-structure constant $\alpha$ but with potentially enhanced kinematic dependence.

Question: Is the inclusion of two-photon exchange contributions in elastic electron–proton scattering quantitatively responsible for the observed discrepancy between $G_E^p/G_M^p$ extracted by the Rosenbluth method and that extracted by the polarization-transfer method?
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical calculations and phenomenological analyses have established that hadronic two-photon exchange corrections, kinematically enhanced in the Rosenbluth method but suppressed in the polarization-transfer method, can largely account for the discrepancy in $G_E^p/G_M^p$ extractions. Three dedicated experiments comparing $e^+p$ and $e^-p$ elastic scattering (VEPP-3, CLAS, OLYMPUS), as well as recent positron-beam Super-Rosenbluth measurements, have confirmed the existence of a small TPE effect of the expected order. However, the precision and kinematic reach remain insufficient to definitively confirm the theoretical treatments or to show that TPE quantitatively closes the discrepancy at all $Q^2$. The question is therefore partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: How to reconcile the Rosenbluth and the polarization transfer methods in the measurement of the proton form factors
status_evidence.snippet: The apparent discrepancy ... can be explained by a two-photon exchange correction ... kinematically enhanced in the Rosenbluth method while it is small for the polarization transfer method.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical TPE corrections can explain the discrepancy.

status_evidence.title: Determination of two-photon exchange via e+p/e-p scattering with CLAS12
status_evidence.snippet: Direct experimental determinations of the TPE contribution via e+p/e-p ratio measurements.
status_evidence.claim: Experiments have tested but not definitively pinned down TPE as the full explanation.

status_evidence.title: A measurement of two-photon exchange in Super-Rosenbluth separations with positron beams
status_evidence.snippet: Results support the existence of a small TPE effect but cannot establish that theoretical treatments are fully valid.
